processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds were moved stepwise inside the furnace and successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; Al was charged through an air lock after each cast.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³-sized blocks were hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Sheets were cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into nine segments of 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Aging was one of nine RAP heat treatments (450/500/550/600 °C for 0/1/24 h).
Low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic microstructure with nm-sized κ-carbide precipitates formed during aging at 550 °C.

precipitates.coherency: coherent (lattice mismatch below 3% with austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Orowan bypassing of longitudinal κ-carbide rods, expansion of dislocation loops assisted by dislocation cross-slip, and minor shearing of κ-carbides.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Dislocation-based strain hardening; after aging at 500–600 °C, twinning is reduced and strain hardening is essentially associated with κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Aging promotes the formation of nm-sized κ-carbides.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine yield strength (YS), ultimate tensile strength (UTS), and total elongation (TE)
characterization_methods.key_findings: For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al, aging for 1 h increases YS, UTS and hardness (increasing with temperature) with only a minor reduction in TE.

characterization_methods.purpose: Screen hardness as a function of Al content and aging condition
characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness rises steeply at 8Al relative to 0–6Al (to about 375 HBW for the strongest condition).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
cross-section perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling and water quenching gave a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al alloy, aging for 1 h leads to an increase in YS, UTS, and hardness (increasing with aging temperature) and only a minor reduction in TE.
The pronounced strengthening of the ~8 wt.% Al variant during aging is attributed to the formation of nm-sized κ-carbides.
In the tensile strength vs elongation plot (Fig. 4), the 8Al (purple) series reaches the highest tensile strength (~800–950 MPa) among the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl alloys.
The Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al alloy is described as the material with the highest Al content and lowest density in the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl set.
After aging at 500–600 °C, twinning is reduced and strain hardening is essentially associated with κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening.

Exact YS/UTS/TE/hardness values for the 550 °C/1 h condition are not individually tabulated in the text; Fig. 3 plots the 550 °C/1 h curve, but numeric callouts are given mainly for the 550 °C/24 h and as-homogenised conditions.
